close_reason: Fixed in commit 247fb69. Added 'Cross-type cascade contract' subsection to ChatBackend::apply_space_patch rustdoc (backend.rs) documenting RemoveChannel cascade to Chat + Message destruction with both type-state-token bumps, RemoveCategory cascade to Chat.categoryId clearing with Chat state bump, RemoveRole cascade to member roleIds (captured by Space bump), and RemoveMember bookkeeping with implementation-defined ReadPosition cleanup. Existing tests at integration.rs:4102-4125 already assert the cascade; the doc gap is now closed.
description:
## Finding

`ChatBackend::apply_space_patch`'s rustdoc
(`crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:441-509`) discusses
ordering, atomicity, permission gates, and per-aggregate count
limits. It is **entirely silent on cross-type cascade behaviour
when destructive ops fire**.

The kit's integration test suite asserts a substantial cascade
contract that the rustdoc does not state.

## Test 1: RemoveChannel cascades to Message destruction with state bump

`crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/integration.rs:4102-4125` asserts
that removing a channel from a Space:

1. Destroys all `Message` records contained in that channel.
2. Bumps the `Message` type's state token so
   `Message/changes` subscribers see the destruction.

Verbatim assertion:

```rust
// ... the only Message state-bump in this run is the
// one our removeChannels cascade emits. So a Message/changes since
// "0" must list exactly m1, m2, m3 in `destroyed`.
// ...
assert_eq!(
    destroyed,
    vec!["m1".to_owned(), "m2".to_owned(), "m3".to_owned()],
    "cascade must destroy exactly the three messages in the removed channel: {destroyed:?}"
);
```

The kitchen-sink test's seeding comment at
`tests/space_set_kitchen_sink.rs:55-60` even acknowledges that
this contract exists only in code, not in docs:

> The reference impl's `apply_space_patch` for `removeChannels`
> cascades to Chat destruction and Message destruction; tests
> in `tests/integration.rs` cover that cascade.

## What goes wrong for a third-party implementer

A third-party backend that implements `RemoveChannel` by deleting
only the Space-side cross-reference (the natural minimal
implementation):

1. **Passes the rustdoc contract** — nothing in `apply_space_patch`'s
   doc mentions cross-type effects.
2. **Leaves orphaned `Chat` and `Message` rows** in the storage
   layer. They become unreachable through Space navigation but
   keep existing as zombie records consuming quota.
3. **Misses the `Message` and `Chat` state-token bumps**, so
   subscribers to `Message/changes` and `Chat/changes` never
   see the removal. The clients' local cache of the removed
   channel's messages remains visible indefinitely.
4. **Diverges from RFC 8620 `/changes` semantics** silently — a
   `since=$state` poll appears to show no change, but a fresh
   `Message/query` shows the messages gone.

This is a substantive correctness gap, not a polish issue. The
failure mode is silent at compile time, silent in single-tenant
smoke tests, and only manifests when a multi-client subscriber
notices their cache went stale.

## Comparison to other documented cascade rules

The same trait DOES extensively document cascade rules
elsewhere:

- `expire_message` at `backend.rs:856-892` — 60 lines on what
  happens when a Message is expired (state token bumps,
  cross-references nulled, etc.).
- `protect_last_admin` at `backend.rs:583-624` — explicit
  contract on the post-mutation member/role graph state.

The asymmetry is striking: the most central destructive backend
method (`apply_space_patch` with `RemoveChannel` /
`RemoveCategory` / `RemoveRole` / `RemoveMember`) has zero
cascade documentation; auxiliary methods have detailed cascade
documentation.

## Recommendation

Add a "Cross-type cascade contract" sub-section to
`apply_space_patch`'s rustdoc. Minimum surface to cover:

- `RemoveChannel`: MUST destroy all `Chat` records associated
  with the channel and all `Message` records contained in those
  chats; MUST bump the `Chat` and `Message` type state tokens.
- `RemoveCategory`: MUST clear `Chat.categoryId` for any chats
  in the destroyed category (see separate finding on the
  category-cascade Chat/changes contract); MUST bump `Chat`
  state.
- `RemoveRole`: MUST clear the role from every `SpaceMember.roleIds`
  in the Space; effects on `SpaceMember/changes` (if the kit
  models members as a separate JMAP type).
- `RemoveMember`: MUST clear the member's `ReadPosition` records
  for any Chats in the Space (or — alternatively — preserve
  them; the kit's intended choice should be stated).

For each cascade target, state whether the state token bump is
required, and whether subscribers should see the cross-type
changes via `<TargetType>/changes`.

## Engineering basis

- Test assertion at `integration.rs:4102-4125` verbatim.
- Seeding comment at `space_set_kitchen_sink.rs:55-60` verbatim.
- Rustdoc at `backend.rs:441-509` read end-to-end; no cascade
  language present.
- The reference impl at `memory.rs` does implement the cascade
  correctly (else the test would fail), so the kit ships a
  cascade-correct reference and a cascade-silent doc — the
  worst combination for third-party implementers.

## Priority justification

P1 because:
- The failure is a multi-type spec-correctness gap (`Message/changes`
  and `Chat/changes` subscribers diverge from query reality).
- The failure is silent at every layer that a third-party
  implementer can reasonably test in isolation (no compile
  error, no panic, no smoke test).
- The fix is doc-only — high leverage, zero code churn.
- Sibling finding (category-cascade Chat/changes) shares the
  same failure mode and same fix.
title: API contract: apply_space_patch RemoveChannel cascade contract entirely undocumented; tests assert cascade destroys Messages and bumps Message state
